blogs.title: Adnexal Mass or Pedunculated Fibroid? The Pregnancy Imaging Trap
blogs.description: This post would unpack how a giant cystic, pedunculated leiomyoma can masquerade as an ovarian mass in the second trimester. It would focus on the bedside and imaging clues that help distinguish degenerating fibroids from endometriomas or adnexal neoplasms, including the value and limitations of bimanual exam, Doppler ultrasound, and non-contrast MRI when the gravid uterus distorts normal anatomy.

blogs.title: CA-125 at 21 Weeks: When a Tumor Marker Creates More Heat Than Light
blogs.description: A practical review of tumor markers in pregnancy, using this case’s mildly rising CA-125 to illustrate how easily clinicians can be misled. The post would discuss trimester-specific physiology, poor specificity for malignancy, the limited role of isolated values, and how to integrate serial markers with imaging and clinical context rather than overreacting to borderline abnormalities.

blogs.title: When to Operate on a Mass in Pregnancy: The Second-Trimester Decision Point
blogs.description: This piece would explore the management tension between conservative care and antepartum surgery for large symptomatic abdominal masses. Using this case, it would frame indications for intervention—pain, dyspnea from mass effect, torsion, rupture, infection risk, or oncologic uncertainty—and discuss why the second trimester is often the least bad time to operate when surgery cannot be avoided.

blogs.title: The Minimalist Pregnant Myomectomy: Resect the Problem, Leave the Risk
blogs.description: A surgical strategy post centered on doing the minimum necessary to preserve pregnancy. It would analyze the intraoperative choice to remove only the twisted, leaking pedunculated myoma while leaving the fixed pelvic mass in situ, and use that decision to discuss hemorrhage avoidance, fetal monitoring during non-obstetric surgery, operative time, anemia/transfusion planning, and the limited evidence behind perioperative progesterone or tocolytic practices.

blogs.title: Fibroids, Scar, and Outlet Obstruction: Planning Delivery After Antepartum Myomectomy
blogs.description: This post would cover how fibroid size, number, and location should drive delivery planning more than dogma. It would use the residual posterior pelvic myoma as a springboard to discuss when vaginal birth is unrealistic, how prior antepartum myomectomy changes thinking about uterine rupture risk, why elective cesarean may be the safer path, and how postpartum fibroid regression can justify deferred definitive surgery.
